theory.intro: A **box plot** (or box-and-whisker plot) shows the five-number summary of a dataset along a scaled number line. The **box** stretches from $Q_1$ to $Q_3$ (the middle $50\%$ of the data), with a line inside it at the **median**. A **whisker** runs from each end of the box out to the minimum or maximum value.
facts: A box plot shows five values: the **minimum**, $Q_1$, the **median** ($Q_2$), $Q_3$, and the **maximum**, marked against a scaled number line.
The **box** runs from $Q_1$ to $Q_3$ — this is the middle $50\%$ of the data, split by a line at the median.
The **left whisker** runs from the minimum to $Q_1$; the **right whisker** runs from $Q_3$ to the maximum.
A box plot needs only a numeric axis in the data's units — there is no frequency axis, because a box plot does not show individual values.
steps: Draw and scale a number line that comfortably fits the minimum to the maximum.
Mark the minimum and maximum with a short vertical whisker end.
Draw a line inside the box at the median.
Join each whisker end to the nearest edge of the box.

foundation.solution_text:
The box of a box plot represents the middle $50\%$ of the data.
It is drawn between $Q_1$ and $Q_3$.

development.solution_text:
A whisker joins a box edge to an extreme value.
The left whisker runs from the minimum up to $Q_1$, the left edge of the box.

mastery.question_text:
A swimmer's start reaction times have minimum $220$ ms and a range of $90$ ms. $Q_1=240$, the median is $255$ and $Q_3=270$.
Find the maximum reaction time, then state the full five-number summary.
